rows.question: Where should I start?

The step to AI comes from the simulation-versus-instantiation section [spya-pbcr03], and his own hedge is at [spya-qu7j89].

rows.text:
Before you decide, note that Seth argues something narrower than "AI can't be conscious." He says it's very unlikely for the digital computers we know, and "nothing in what I've said rules out the possibility of artificial consciousness altogether" [spya-rn8y3y].

Skim the opening and the section on psychological biases. Read closely from the claim he's attacking, computational functionalism [spya-wepmnr], through his four arguments. Then read where he admits he might be wrong [spya-qu7j89].

Ideas lists the assumptions each side needs, so you can see which ones you'd accept.
